q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries compute the average experience years of employees assigned to each project, grouping by PROJECT_ID and rounding to two decimal places. The only difference is the use of aliases (A and B for Q1, P and E for Q2), which does not affect the result.
